title: Robotic aortic valve replacement with a sutureless valve, through a 3 cm transaxillary incision: a step-by-step surgical guide.
authors: Saurabh Varshney; Shreya Varshney; Manish Sonkusale
journal: Multimedia manual of cardiothoracic surgery : MMCTS
abstract: Robotic aortic valve replacement remains a challenging procedure, limiting its widespread adoption. We present our technique of robotic aortic valve replacement with da Vinci X system, with a sutureless valve (Perceval Plus), where we have tried to simplify the procedural steps. These can be very easily adopted by surgeons worldwide. The procedure includes port placement, docking, incision planning, femoral cannulation, aortotomy, valve excision, implantation tips for the sutureless valve, and aortotomy closure. The refinement of this approach has been associated with rapid postoperative recovery, with the patient walking in less than 24 hours after surgery. This step-by-step video tutorial will help surgeons worldwide in the adoption of robotic aortic valve replacement techniques.

title: Bicuspidization of a severely dysplastic aortic valve in a neonate.
authors: Ivan Kozyrev; Mathieu Vergnat; Philipp Suchowerskyj; Benjamin Bierbach; Claudia Arenz; Boulos Asfour
journal: Multimedia manual of cardiothoracic surgery : MMCTS
abstract: Severe congenital aortic valve stenosis in neonates remains a challenging lesion requiring individualized treatment. While balloon aortic valvuloplasty and surgical valvotomy are established treatment options, neonates with severely dysplastic valve morphology may benefit from anatomical valve reconstruction in addition to relief of obstruction. This video tutorial demonstrates our technique of bicuspidization of a severely dysplastic neonatal aortic valve by commissural reconstruction, extensive leaflet shaving and limited free-edge remodelling. Our ultimate goal of tricuspid valve repair was impossible in this scenario.

title: Transaxillary direct-view aortic valve replacement with Intuity Elite rapid-deployment valve.
authors: Michele Galeazzi; Erlil Mali; Simone D'Alessio; Martina Giusti; Carlo Zingaro; Pietro Malvindi; Paolo Berretta; Marco Di Eusanio
journal: Multimedia manual of cardiothoracic surgery : MMCTS
abstract: We present a minimally invasive aortic valve replacement performed through a right transaxillary minithoracotomy. This approach uses a single 4-5 cm lateral incision, minimizing chest wall trauma while providing excellent cosmetic results. It redefines surgical perspective by offering a direct, non-mediated view of the aortic valve with a naturally perpendicular trajectory to the annular plane. This results in optimal eye-hand alignment, shorter working distance and enhanced operative control, simplifying the procedure, not only compared to endoscopic or robotic techniques, but also to right anterior minithoracotomy, where direct vision is obtained through a less favourable trajectory and a more limited anterior intercostal space. The procedure is performed using standard instruments and standardized set-up, without the need for specialized or expensive technologies, improving reproducibility and scalability. Its intrinsic simplicity makes it particularly suited for fast-track protocols, facilitating on-table extubation and early mobilization. The combination with rapid-deployment valves further streamlines the operation by reducing cardiopulmonary bypass and cross-clamp times, while the transaxillary exposure ensures accurate annular alignment and controlled, symmetrical deployment. In this case, the patient was extubated on-table and discharged home after 5 days, illustrating how this approach can simplify minimally invasive aortic valve surgery while maintaining safety and precision.

title: Aortic Root Remodeling Patterns and Outcomes Five Years Following Contemporary Root Replacement Strategies in Young Patients: A Single-Center Experience.
authors: Obieze Nwanna-Nzewunwa; Mayowa Otoruko; Robert D B Jaquiss; Nicholas D Andersen; Ryan R Davies; Karl M Reyes
journal: World journal for pediatric & congenital heart surgery
abstract: Background: Long-term dimensional remodeling patterns after contemporary aortic root operations in young patients have historically not been well characterized and this may inform surgical decision-making.Methods: We evaluated longitudinal aortic root and annular remodeling patterns and clinical outcomes after the Bentall, Ross, or Valve-Sparing Root procedures from January 1, 2000 to December 31, 2024.Results: Sixty patients underwent aortic root replacement. Of these, 17 had the Bentall procedure (BP), 20 had the Ross procedure, and 23 had Valve Sparing Aortic Root Replacement (VSARR). On average Ross patients (4 years) were younger than BP (16 years) and VSARR (16 years) (p = .0001). Marfans (20%, 12/60), Down Syndrome (3%, 2/60) and Loeys-Dietz (3%, 2/60) were prevalent. All Marfan patients (n = 12) underwent VSARR (p = .006). The leading surgical indications were aortic regurgitation (78%, 47/60), aortic stenosis (58%, 35/60), and aortic aneurysm (46%, 28/60). Mortality rate was 7% (n = 4/60) and no statistically significant difference in survival was observed (p = .94). Reoperation occurred in 3 of 60 patients (5%). Four of 60 patients (7%) had endocarditis. At 5 years, the change in aortic root size was significantly different across operation types (p = .041), with significant dilation noted in the Ross cohort.Conclusions: Ross patients demonstrated greater neoaortic root enlargement at 5 years, although valve competence was generally preserved. Given the differences in age, underlying pathology, and surgical selection among the groups, these findings should be interpreted as descriptive remodeling patterns rather than evidence of the superiority of one operative strategy.

title: Pooled Periprocedural and Short-Term Outcomes After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement With Contemporary Self-Expanding Valves: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Shawn Shaji; Praveen Bharath Saravanan; Rahul Sarkar; Chloe Kharsa; Joe Aoun; Syed Zaid; Waleed T Kayani; Nadeen Faza; Stephen H Little; Marvin Atkins; Fernando Ramirez Del Val; Neal S Kleiman; Michael J Reardon; Sahar Samimi; Sachin S Goel
journal: Structural heart : the journal of the Heart Team
abstract:
Contemporary self-expanding transcatheter heart valves (SEVs) have incorporated design refinements to reduce paravalvular leak (PVL) and pacemaker implantation (PPI). We aimed to characterize clinical outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) with contemporary SEVs in patients with severe aortic stenosis.
PubMed, EMBASE, and Scopus were searched through October 5, 2025, for studies reporting procedural, hemodynamic, and clinical outcomes for patients undergoing TAVR with the (1) Navitor or (2) Evolut PRO/PRO+/FX. Random-effects meta-analyses pooled single-arm event rates, stratified by SEV group, using the Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation. Between-platform differences were assessed using subgroup interaction testing.
Fifty-two studies (n = 21,349; weighted mean age 82 years; mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality 4.8%) were included. At 30 days, all-cause mortality was low among Evolut and Navitor cohorts (1.4 and 1.5%; p = 0.63), and device success was high for both platforms (92.1 and 93.0%; p = 0.73). Moderate or greater PVL occurred in 2.5 and 1.1% of Evolut and Navitor cohorts, respectively (p = 0.12), mild PVL occurred in 31.1 and 19.9% (p = 0.046), and new PPI occurred in 13.4 and 15.3%, respectively. Mean gradients remained low among Evolut and Navitor cohorts at 1 year (7.7 and 7.3 mmHg; p = 0.65), whereas effective orifice area was higher among Evolut cohorts at 1 year (2.1 and 1.8 cm2; p < 0.001) (p = p-interaction).
Navitor and Evolut PRO/PRO+/FX both demonstrated high device success, low mortality, favorable hemodynamic performance, and low rates of moderate or greater PVL at 1-year follow-up. Mild PVL and new PPI remained frequent. Observed comparative signals should be interpreted as indirect hypothesis-generating findings.

title: Giant hiatal hernia as a contributing physiological stressor to cardiopulmonary dysfunction: a case report.
authors: Michelle Carrasquel-Alvarez; Mariana Valdez-Thomas; Maria Del Pilar Acosta
abstract:
Extracardiac thoracic pathology can significantly alter cardiac physiology and mimic primary heart disease, particularly in older adults with multiple comorbidities.
An 89-year-old woman with known aortic stenosis and heart failure presented with 1 week of progressive, positional dyspnoea and wheezing. Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated severe global left ventricular systolic dysfunction with an estimated ejection fraction of approximately 30%, a dilated left atrium (dimension 4.77 cm, volume 100 mL), and markedly elevated filling pressures evidenced by a medial e' velocity of 3.16 cm/s, mitral E velocity of 103 cm/s, and E/e' ratio of 32.6. Aortic valve assessment revealed haemodynamic features of low-flow, low-gradient severe aortic stenosis, with a mean gradient of 26-28 mmHg, a valve area of 0.68 cm by continuity equation, a dimensionless index of 0.25, and a stroke volume index of 29.4 mL/m2. Notably, right ventricular size and systolic function were preserved despite estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure of 40-45 mmHg, a pattern physiologically discordant with the degree of left-sided dysfunction. Chest computed tomography revealed a giant paraesophageal hiatal hernia measuring 10-12 cm, with intrathoracic migration of the stomach causing extrinsic compression of the left atrium and posterior cardiac structures. Troponin was negative, and no electrocardiographic evidence of acute ischaemia was identified. The observed left ventricular dysfunction is likely multifactorial, with extracardiac compression acting as a contributing physiological stressor in the context of underlying low-flow severe aortic stenosis.
This case highlights the importance of recognizing extracardiac causes of cardiopulmonary deterioration and integrating multimodality imaging into diagnostic reasoning, particularly when haemodynamic findings are physiologically discordant.

title: Quantitative membranous septum area assessment with advanced three-dimensional CT visualization with a mixed reality-capable device.
authors: Cian O'Sullivan; Tsung-Ying Tsai; Hao-Wei Lee; Fei-Ran Chiou; Rachel Beatty; Maciej Stanuch; Andrzej Skalski; Akihiro Tobe; Garry P Duffy; Brendan Wilkins; Ryo Torii; Nicolo Piazza; Yoshinobu Onuma; Patrick W Serruys
abstract:
Permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI) rates remained elevated for patients receiving transcatheter aortic valve implantation for aortic stenosis (AS) and aortic regurgitation. Therefore, detailed assessment of the membranous septum (MS) anatomy is essential to understand the mechanism and mitigate risk. This study aims to examine the accuracy and reproducibility of a novel 3D hologram system to measure transcatheter aortic valve implantation-related aortic valvar complex anatomy and present a novel methodology to measure MS area with it.
Cardiac computer tomography series of AS, aortic regurgitation, and coronary artery disease (CAD) patient cohorts were analysed using CarnaLife Holo (MedApp SA, Kraków, Poland) to quantify and compare their MS areas. 3mensio Structural Heart was used as a benchmark comparator, with annulus area (AA) selected as the quantitative parameter. Intraclass correlation coefficient values between the software all exceeded 0.99, with no statistically significant difference noted between AA measurements. Bland-Altman plotting illustrated narrow boundaries of agreement, with no significant outliers. In interobserver agreement analysis for 3D hologram, AA measurements were not significantly different between two investigators (P = 0.906). No significant difference was found between the MS areas between the three cohorts after ANOVA testing (P = 0.1640).
3D holographic software provides a feasible and reproducible tool for visualising and measuring the aortic valvar complex anatomy. In addition, its ability to assess the shape, pattern, and area of the MS offers anatomic insights not readily available with other software.

title: Navigating Severe Aortic Stenosis in Hip Fracture Surgery: Perioperative Management and Surgical Timing.
authors: Richard Bui; Jen Li Dong; Austin Tran; Laasya Achanta; Jamal Hasoon; Alaa Abd-Elsayed; Alan D Kaye; Anvinh Nguyen
abstract: Severe aortic stenosis presents a significant challenge in patients requiring urgent hip fracture surgery. Although aortic stenosis increases the risk of cardiovascular complications and mortality, delaying fixation may independently contribute to morbidity, functional decline, and mortality. This creates a dilemma regarding whether to proceed directly to surgery or delay fracture repair for aortic valve intervention. This review examines management of patients with severe aortic stenosis pending urgent hip fracture surgery, with emphasis on timing, preoperative evaluation, anesthetic selection, and hemodynamic management. Current evidence suggests that asymptomatic patients with preserved left ventricular systolic function and stable hemodynamics may often undergo timely fracture fixation with appropriate monitoring. In contrast, symptomatic patients, those with ventricular dysfunction or hemodynamic instability, and patients with particularly severe disease may require evaluation for valvular intervention. When intervention is indicated, transcatheter aortic valve replacement may offer a more rapid treatment in certain patients, while balloon aortic valvuloplasty may serve as a temporizing strategy. For patients proceeding directly to fracture fixation, preservation of preload, systemic vascular resistance, coronary perfusion, and sinus rhythm is essential. Current evidence does not establish a clear superiority of general versus neuraxial anesthesia, supporting individualized anesthetic planning and avoidance of abrupt hemodynamic changes. Ultimately, management should balance the risks of delaying fracture fixation against the risks of surgery through coordinated, multidisciplinary decision-making.

title: Severe Calcific Aortic Stenosis in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: A Case Report and Literature Review.
authors: Abeer Omar; Aya Abdelhamid; Abdallah Elsukkar; Mohammed Altermanini
journal: Heart views : the official journal of the Gulf Heart Association
abstract: Severe calcific aortic stenosis (CAS) in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is exceptionally rare. SLE affects multiple organ systems, including the cardiovascular system. Cardiovascular mortality in SLE is approximately three times higher than in the general population, and cardiovascular morbidity affects about 25% of patients. Although valvular heart disease (VHD) is common in SLE, marked aortic stenosis, particularly severe CAS, remains uncommon. This case report describes a 60-year-old female patient with SLE and VHD who developed rapid progressive, severe, symptomatic CAS. A multidisciplinary heart team determined that she was at prohibitive risk for surgical aortic valve replacement, and she subsequently underwent high-risk transcatheter aortic valve implantation. No SLE flare occurred. Regular cardiovascular risk assessment and echocardiographic screening are essential for patients with SLE. Careful multidisciplinary and immunosuppressive management supports successful interventions while minimizing the risk of SLE flare.

title: Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation-Induced Right Hepatic Lobe Laceration Causing Delayed 5,500mL Hemoperitoneum During Post-resuscitation Anticoagulation: A Case Report.
authors: Hideo Kidogawa; Nobutaka Matayoshi; Takatomo Yamayoshi; Masao Inoue; Yuki Tsuda
abstract: Closed-chest cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) can induce rare, life-threatening intra-abdominal visceral injuries. We report a case of CPR-induced liver laceration leading to delayed massive intra-abdominal hemorrhage (5,500 mL) in a 40-year-old male patient with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) due to severe left main coronary artery (LMCA) stenosis. Following the return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) achieved 32 minutes after collapse (28 minutes of CPR), the patient was managed with an intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP), systemic unfractionated heparin, and targeted temperature management (TTM at 34°C). On post-resuscitation day 2 during rewarming, the patient developed delayed hemorrhagic shock and marked abdominal distension, with hemoglobin plunging from 16.3 g/dL to 7.5 g/dL. Dynamic contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) demonstrated massive hemoperitoneum without active arterial extravasation (blush). Following emergent blood transfusion and volume resuscitation, exploratory laparotomy evacuated 5,500 mL of dark blood and identified a deep capsule laceration on the visceral surface of the right hepatic lobe adjacent to the gallbladder attachment site with continuous venous oozing. Direct parenchymal suturing, cholecystectomy, and topical application of human fibrinogen/thrombin-coated collagen fleece (TachoComb) achieved complete hemostasis. The patient was successfully weaned from IABP on postoperative day 1 and transferred for elective coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG) with complete neurological recovery (Cerebral Performance Category 1). In post-resuscitation patients under systemic anticoagulation and suspected hypothermia-associated coagulopathy, delayed shock must immediately raise suspicion of visceral trauma. The absence of arterial blush on dynamic CT does not exclude life-threatening venous oozing, and prompt open laparotomy with direct mechanical hemostasis represents a life-saving intervention.

title: Management of bicuspid aortic stenosis.
authors: Daryoush Samim; Matthias Siepe; Mevlüt Çelik; Ole De Backer; Michael A Borger; Stephan Windecker
journal: European heart journal. Valvular and structural heart disease
abstract:
Bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) disease is the most common congenital heart lesion and is associated with premature leaflet degeneration, aortic stenosis (AS), aortic regurgitation (AR), endocarditis, and ascending aortic pathologies. This review aims to summarize the key issues frequently associated with BAV and their impact on treatment decision-making, with a particular focus on surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) versus transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) in patients presenting with AS.
Patients with BAV experience a 70% lifetime risk of aortic valve surgery, often at a younger age than those with a trileaflet anatomy. BAV is present in up to 40% of patients undergoing SAVR, which remains the standard of care in low-risk patients. TAVI has emerged as a less invasive treatment alternative with favorable short- and mid-term outcomes in appropriately selected BAV patients. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing TAVI and SAVR have systematically excluded BAV patients, except for the UK TAVI trial and recent NOTION-2 trial, the latter signalling a potentially increased risk of all-cause mortality, stroke, and re-hospitalization rates at 1 year among low-risk BAV patients undergoing TAVI. Dedicated RCTs comparing TAVI and SAVR for BAV stenosis are in preparation and will inform future guidelines.
Treatment decisions for BAV patients should be individualized by Heart Teams, considering periprocedural risk, comorbidities, aortic root anatomy, and life expectancy. Future trials in this specific population will clarify the optimal role of TAVI and SAVR in managing BAV-related aortic stenosis.

title: 2025 ESC/EACTS Guidelines for the management of valvular heart disease: Developed by the task force for the management of valvular heart disease of the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) and the European Association for Cardio-Thoracic Surgery (EACTS).

title: Validation of the British Cardiovascular Intervention Society Jeopardy Score from coronary CT angiography in TAVI candidates.
authors: Anastasia Fiechtner; Raffael Ghenzi; Claudio Bruker; Patric Biaggi; Andreas A Giannopoulos; Oliver Gaemperli
journal: European heart journal. Imaging methods and practice
abstract:
Severe aortic stenosis and coronary artery disease (CAD) frequently coexist in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). The British Cardiovascular Intervention Society Jeopardy Score (BCIS-JS) is a well-established score for determining CAD extent and jeopardized myocardium. The aim of the present study was to validate a CT-derived BCIS-JS (CT-BCIS-JS) against invasive angiography-derived BCIS-JS (iBCIS-JS) in TAVI candidates.
A total of 108 patients (median age 84 years, 43% female) undergoing CCTA prior to TAVI were included. CT-BCIS-JS and iBCIS-JS were both calculated and compared to each other with Spearman rank correlation and Bland-Altman analysis. Diagnostic performance of CT-BCIS-JS for detecting extensive CAD (iBCIS-JS ≥ 6) was assessed using sensitivity, specificity, and positive and negative predictive values, and agreement was evaluated using Cohen's kappa (κ). Correlation between CT-BCIS-JS and iBCIS-JS was good (Spearman's rho = 0.61). Bland-Altman analysis demonstrated systematic overestimation of BCIS-JS with CT (by an average of 2.2 units) with rather wide limits of agreement (-4.6-9.1). A CT-BCIS-JS ≥ 6 had excellent sensitivity and negative predictive value (93% and 99%, respectively) to detect extensive CAD on invasive angiography, but moderate to low specificity and positive predictive value (76% and 39%, respectively), and agreement for dichotomized BCIS-JS was moderate (κ = 0.44).
CT-BCIS-JS may serve as a reliable rule-out tool for extensive CAD, potentially reducing the need for invasive angiography in selected TAVI candidates, although systematic overestimation limits its rule-in capability.

title: Prognostic impact of domiciliary care prior to transcatheter aortic valve implantation: a nationwide study.
authors: Victoria Mikkelsen; Jeppe K Petersen; Martha Meibom; Louise Marqvard Sørensen; Morten Schou; Jonas Agerlund Povlsen; Christian Juhl Terkelsen; Ashkan Eftekhari; Henrik Nissen; Ole de Backer; Lars Køber; Emil Fosbøl
journal: European heart journal. Valvular and structural heart disease
abstract:
Domiciliary care can serve as a marker of frailty and vulnerability, which may influence outcomes following transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). The relationship between receipt of domiciliary care prior to TAVI and clinical outcomes has not been systematically evaluated and may influence patient selection and pre-procedural counselling.
The study population included all adult patients with a diagnosis of aortic stenosis undergoing first-time TAVI from 1 January 2015, to 31 December 2023. Patients were categorized into those with and without domiciliary care within 1 year prior to TAVI. Patients were followed for 1 year after TAVI. All-cause mortality was assessed using Kaplan-Meier estimates and multivariable Cox proportional hazards models. Cumulative days of hospitalization within 1 year after TAVI were calculated and categorized as 0-14 days and >14 days. The association between domiciliary care and >14 cumulative days of hospitalization was evaluated using multivariable logistic regression.
We identified 7607 patients undergoing TAVI, 541 (7.1%) with domiciliary care (76.7% living alone; 39.4% men; median age 83 years) and 7066 (92.9%) without domiciliary care (40.5% living alone; 59.4% men; median age 81 years). Overall, patients with domiciliary care carried a higher comorbidity burden and were more frequently classified in higher frailty groups. From discharge, the absolute 1-year risk of death was 21.5% in patients with domiciliary care and 6.4% in patients without. In adjusted analysis, patients with domiciliary care had an increased associated 1-year mortality [hazard ratio 3.30; 95% confidence interval (CI) 2.65-4.10, P < .0001] compared to those without domiciliary care. Domiciliary care was also associated with higher odds of >14 cumulative days of hospitalization (reference 0-14 days), within 1 year after TAVI (odds ratio 2.94; 95% CI 2.41-3.59, P < .0001).
Patients receiving domiciliary care before undergoing TAVI had a higher mortality and cumulative days of hospitalization within 1 year following the procedure, highlighting a high-risk group of patients. More research is needed to improve risk stratification of TAVI patients.

title: Assessing the impact of age on outcomes following percutaneous coronary intervention in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement-a substudy in NOTION-3.
authors: Klara E Nygaard; Burcu Tas Özbek; Muhammad Sabbah; Reza Jabbari; Charlotte Glinge; Karsten T Veien; Matti Niemela; Phillip Freeman; Rickard Linder; Dan Ioanes; Christian J Terkelsen; Olli A Kajander; Sasha Koul; Mikko Savontaus; Rikke Sørensen; Evald H Christiansen; Pasi Karjalainen; Andrejs Erglis; Jasmine M Marquard; Lars Sondergaard; Ole De Backer; Thomas Engstrøm; Jacob Lønborg
journal: European heart journal. Valvular and structural heart disease
abstract:
Findings from the recent NOTION-3 trial suggest that percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) improves outcomes in patients with severe aortic stenosis and concomitant coronary artery disease undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). Whether the benefit of PCI is consistent across age groups is uncertain.
To investigate the impact of age on outcomes from NOTION-3.
A secondary analysis of 455 patients in the NOTION-3 trial, a randomized trial comparing PCI with conservative treatment in patients with aortic stenosis and coronary artery disease undergoing TAVI. Patients were stratified into four age groups based on the quartile distribution of age (<78, 78-81, 82-84, and ≥85 years) and followed for a median of 2 years (IQR: 1-4 years). The primary outcome was major adverse cardiac events defined as a composite of all-cause death, myocardial infarction, or urgent revascularization.
The risk difference for the primary endpoint comparing PCI and conservative treatment was most pronounced in patients aged 78-81 years [17% vs 42%; hazard ratio (HR): 0.36, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.17-0.77, P = .008]. For the age groups <78, 82-84 and ≥85 years this risk difference between treatment groups was (HR: 1.08, 95% CI: 0.48-2.40), (HR: 0.69, 95% CI: 0.35-1.35), and (HR: 0.90, 95% CI: 0.50-1.62), respectively.
In patients with coronary artery disease undergoing TAVI the benefit of PCI compared with conservative treatment on the composite of all-cause death, myocardial infarction, or urgent revascularization was most pronounced among patients aged 78-84 years.

title: Causes of death in severe aortic stenosis according to symptoms and initial treatment strategies in the TAVR era.
authors: Ko Yamamoto; Yasuaki Takeji; Tomohiko Taniguchi; Takeshi Morimoto; Shinichi Shirai; Takeshi Kitai; Hiroyuki Tabata; Nobuhisa Ohno; Ryosuke Murai; Kohei Osakada; Koichiro Murata; Masanao Nakai; Hiroshi Tsuneyoshi; Tomohisa Tada; Masashi Amano; Shin Watanabe; Hiroki Shiomi; Hirotoshi Watanabe; Yusuke Yoshikawa; Ryusuke Nishikawa; Yuki Obayashi; Eri Minamino-Muta; Mamoru Toyofuku; Shojiro Tatsushima; Norio Kanamori; Makoto Miyake; Hiroyuki Nakayama; Kazuya Nagao; Masayasu Izuhara; Kenji Nakatsuma; Moriaki Inoko; Takanari Fujita; Masahiro Kimura; Mitsuru Ishii; Shunsuke Usami; Fumiko Nakazeki; Kiyonori Togi; Yasutaka Inuzuka; Kenji Ando; Tatsuhiko Komiya; Koh Ono; Kenji Minatoya; Takeshi Kimura
journal: European heart journal. Valvular and structural heart disease
abstract:
There are no studies evaluating mortality and causes of death in severe aortic stenosis (AS) according to symptoms and treatment strategies in contemporary transcatheter aortic valve replacement era.
Among 3369 consecutive patients with severe AS in the CURRENT AS registry-2, we comprehensively evaluated mortality rates and causes of death in patients with severe AS according to symptoms and treatment strategies.
There were 2011 patients with symptomatic severe AS [initial aortic valve replacement (AVR) strategy: N = 1410, and conservative strategy: N = 601] and 1358 patients with asymptomatic severe AS (initial AVR strategy: N = 332, and conservative strategy: N = 1026). During median 2.2 years follow-up, all-cause death occurred in 736 patients, including 297 patients with cardiac death (40.4% of total mortality), 44 patients with vascular death (6.0% of total mortality), and 351 patients with non-cardiovascular death (47.7% of total mortality). In patients with cardiac death, the most common cause was heart failure (22.6% of total mortality), and the second most common cause was sudden death (11.7% of total mortality). In patients with non-cardiovascular death, the most common cause was infection (19.3% of total mortality), and the second most common cause was malignancy (12.2% of total mortality). Cumulative 3-year incidence of all-cause death (proportions of cardiac and non-cardiovascular death) was 22.9% (30.2% and 58.2% of total mortality) in symptomatic severe AS with initial AVR strategy, 53.1% (56.1% and 35.6% of total mortality) in symptomatic severe AS with conservative strategy, 15.5% (23.7% and 68.4% of total mortality) in asymptomatic severe AS with initial AVR strategy, and 24.7% (35.7% and 46.9% of total mortality) in asymptomatic severe AS with conservative strategy.
There was a great difference in mortality and causes of death according to symptoms and treatment strategies in severe AS. Non-cardiovascular death was one of the major components of death in patients who were managed not only invasively but also conservatively.

title: Prognostic impact of kidney function before transcatheter aortic valve implantation: A nationwide study.
authors: Martha Meibom; Jeppe K Petersen; Victoria Mikkelsen; Louise Marqvard Sørensen; Jonas Agerlund Povlsen; Christian Juhl Terkelsen; Ashkan Eftekhari; Ole de Backer; Morten Schou; Lars Køber; Emil Fosbøl
journal: European heart journal. Valvular and structural heart disease
abstract:
Prognosis after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) keeps improving, yet some high-risk groups persist, with chronic kidney disease being one. Contemporary data on the prognostic importance of pre-TAVI kidney function are sparse, leaving uncertainty regarding which patients derive limited benefit from TAVI.
To assess the association between pre-procedural kidney function and long-term outcomes in TAVI patients.
We used Danish nationwide registries to identify patients with aortic stenosis undergoing TAVI between 2015 and 2022. Patients were categorized by baseline eGFR into ≥60, 30-59, and <30 mL/min/1.73 m2 or recent dialysis. We examined one-year all-cause mortality and hospitalization burden after TAVI and estimated relative risks using multivariable Cox and logistic regression.
We included 3888 (60.7%) patients with eGFR ≥60 (58.4% male; median age, 80 years), 2185 (34.1%) with eGFR 30-59 (55.5% male; median age, 83), and 336 (5.2%) with eGFR <30 or recent dialysis (58.0% male; median age, 81).One-year cumulative incidence of all-cause mortality was 5.6% for eGFR ≥60, 9.1% for eGFR 30-59, and 19.6% for eGFR <30 or dialysis. Adjusted hazard ratio was significantly higher for eGFR 30-59 (aHR, 1.45; 95% CI, 1.19-1.78, p =0 .0003) and eGFR <30 or dialysis (aHR, 3.07; 95% CI, 2.32-4.08, p < .0001) than eGFR ≥60. Cumulative rehospitalization exceding14 days after TAVI was most frequent among patients with eGFR <30 or dialysis (18.4%).
We observed a stepwise association between pre-TAVI kidney function and post-TAVI one-year mortality as well as hospitalization burden. Kidney impairment potentially has substantial prognostic impact and should be incorporated into lifetime management of patients undergoing TAVI.

title: Post-dilatation using the balloon-expandable valve delivery balloon with same volume (double-tap) to optimize transcatheter aortic valve expansion.
authors: Annette Maznyczka; Samuel Norman; Noman Ali; Michael S Cunnington; Christopher J Malkin; Ole De Backer; Daniel J Blackman
journal: European heart journal. Valvular and structural heart disease
abstract:
Transcatheter heart valve (THV) underexpansion is associated with haemodynamic valve deterioration. Double inflation of balloon-expandable valves using the delivery balloon with unchanged volume (double-tap) may improve THV expansion, while minimizing the risk of complications.
To evaluate the efficacy of double-tap after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) with SAPIEN-3 Ultra RESILIA (S3UR) valves.
This observational study included consecutive patients who underwent TAVI for severe native aortic stenosis and had same-volume double-tap, from November 2024 to September 2025. THV expansion and deformation were assessed fluoroscopically before and after double-tap after appropriate calibration. Thirty-day clinical outcomes were reported.
Of 113 patients who underwent TAVI with same-volume double-tap (mean age: 79.3 ± 7.3 years, 26.5% female, 13.3% bicuspid anatomy), the median THV expansion before double-tap, at the inflow, mid-portion, and outflow was 88.6% (IQR: 86.4-90.4%), 80.1% (IQR: 77.3-82.3%), and 90.1% (IQR: 88.4-90.9%) respectively, and after double-tap increased to 96.4% (IQR: 94.6-98.4%), 90.8% (IQR: 88.6-92.9%), and 97.6% (IQR: 96.3-99.0%) (all P < .001). The largest increase in expansion following double-tap occurred in the THV mid-portion (median: 10.6% [IQR: 9.8-11.6%]). Multivariable predictors of the extent of minimum expansion improvement following double-tap were bicuspid anatomy (P = .005) and aortic valve calcium volume of >385 mm3 (median) (P = .046). The median THV deformation index decreased from 1.05 (IQR: 1.04-1.07) to 1.03 (IQR: 1.02-1.04) after double-tap (P < .001). Thirty-day mortality rate was 0.9%.
Routine double-tap post-dilatation of balloon-expandable valves improves THV expansion and frame deformation, without any clear safety signal. Bicuspid anatomy and aortic valve calcium burden predicted the extent of expansion improvement.

title: Comparison of health status after TAVI and SAVR in younger low-risk patients with aortic stenosis: a NOTION-2 analysis.
authors: Aekapat Phoksiri; Annette Maznyczka; Mikko Savontaus; Arif Khokhar; Øyvind Bleie; Mariann Tang; Oskar Angerås; Matti Niemela; Ingibjörg J Gudmundsdóttir; Ulrik Sartipy; Yusuke Kobari; Mika Laine; Andreas Rück; Jarkko Piuhola; Evald H Christiansen; Markus Malmberg; Rune Haaverstad; Bernard Prendergast; Lars Sondergaard; Hans Gustav Hørsted Thyregod; Troels Højsgaard Jørgensen; Ole De Backer
journal: European heart journal. Valvular and structural heart disease
abstract:
Several trials have shown that transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) and surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) yield non-inferior short- and mid-term clinical outcomes in low surgical risk patients. However, information on the health status achieved by these patients is lacking.
To compare the incidence of excellent health status after TAVI versus SAVR in younger, low-risk patients at 3-year follow-up.
Aortic stenosis (AS) patients aged 60-75 years with low surgical risk (n = 370) were randomised to TAVI or SAVR. For this pre-defined NOTION-2 analysis, the primary safety endpoint was freedom from all-cause mortality and disabling stroke at 3 years. The primary efficacy endpoint was excellent health status, defined as Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ) score >90 and New York Heart Association (NYHA) class I at 3 years.
Three-year follow-up data were available for 341 patients, with health status missing in 4.3% of SAVR and 1.6% of TAVI patients. The primary safety and efficacy endpoints were comparable between TAVI and SAVR (94.6% vs 95.1%, P = .9; and 50.0% vs 45.0%, P = .35, respectively). Among patients with chronic lung disease, bicuspid AS, coronary artery disease, reduced left ventricular systolic function, or prior stroke, non-significant trends suggested a better health status following TAVI, with % risk differences of +10.5%, +13.9%, +16.0%, +18.9%, and +19.7%, respectively; however, these differences did not reach statistical significance.
After 3 years, half of AS patients achieved excellent health status, regardless of TAVI or SAVR. Nonetheless, certain comorbidities predict less improvement in health status, particularly following SAVR.

title: Reading the night between the epochs: continuous decoding of sleep microstructure.
authors: Samaneh Nasiri; Robert J Thomas

title: FDPT-Net (feature focusing diffusion pyramid and task-aligned network): A train wheelset tread detection network based on feature focusing diffusion pyramid and dynamic task alignment.
authors: Kelin Wu; Dan Wang; Yupeng Yao
abstract: Defect detection on train wheel treads is a critical link in ensuring railway transportation safety. Existing deep learning detection models often suffer from scale misalignment and feature information loss during feature fusion, leading to insufficient perception of low-contrast edges in early-stage defects. To address these issues, this paper proposes a train wheel tread defect detection network based on a feature focusing diffusion pyramid network and dynamic task alignment. The network employs StarNet as its backbone to reduce computational cost for deployment on embedded devices. To resolve the problems of scale mismatch and insufficient semantic expression capability among feature maps from different levels, a texture and boundary aware focus module is designed to effectively enhance feature representation. A scale-adaptive dynamic feature extraction module, C3k2-SD-DWR, is adopted to improve the model's capability to extract features of targets at different scales. The model integrates a task align dynamic detection head to enhance the spatial adaptability of features for tread defects. Experimental results on public datasets show that the proposed method achieves an average recognition accuracy of 95.41%, which is 4.9% higher than that of the original model, while reducing model size and computational cost by 1.8 MB and 0.3 GFLOPS, respectively, providing an efficient solution for automated detection of train wheel tread defects.

title: Deep-learning-based underwater target recognition: A multi-cycle range-bearing image fusion approach.
authors: Tianfeng Huang; Kun Wu; Tianming Ye; Xin Yao; Mei Li; Miao Guo
journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
abstract: We propose a multi-cycle range-bearing image-fusion-based deep-learning framework for underwater target recognition. Within this framework, two multi-cycle image construction strategies are developed: multi-cycle temporal accumulation (MCTA) and multi-cycle spatial concatenation (MCSC), which jointly encode traditional target characteristics, including intensity, spatial scale, and motion-related information. Their recognition performance was systematically evaluated under varying signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions. Results show that both MCTA and MCSC achieve competitive recognition performance compared with single-cycle data under high-SNR conditions. However, under low-SNR conditions, MCSC outperforms MCTA by preserving target structural variations and suppressing background clutter. Recognition accuracy increases with the number of fused cycles and reaches 94.55% when 20 cycles are used. Model interpretability was further investigated using gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) and t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE) analyses. t-SNE visualization results show that multi-cycle range-bearing image fusion produces feature representations with larger inter-class separability and more compact intra-category distributions than those obtained from single-cycle images. Grad-CAM results indicate that compared with single-cycle images, 20-cycle MCSC images guide the model to focus more consistently on target-related regions while suppressing responses to background clutter and environmental interference. These findings demonstrate that spatial concatenation effectively aggregates multi-cycle target information, providing a robust and interpretable approach for underwater target recognition under different SNR conditions.

title: G4SAINT enables interpretable prediction of RNA G-quadruplex binding proteins across the human proteome via domain-guided learning.
authors: Nan Weng; Dapeng Xiong; Huiling Shu; Tiantong Tao; Xiao Sun
abstract: RNA G-quadruplexes (RG4s) are noncanonical four-stranded RNA structures that regulate post-transcriptional processes and are linked to multiple diseases, yet identifying their binding proteins remains experimentally challenging and computationally limited. Here, we present G4SAINT, a deep learning framework that predicts RG4-binding potential directly from protein sequence, structural, and domain-guided features. G4SAINT integrates residue-level embeddings from protein language models with graph neural networks and domain-guided attention to capture complementary signals across modalities. Across multiple benchmarks, G4SAINT outperforms existing approaches and accurately highlights regions associated with RG4 recognition. By leveraging multi-task learning across related binding prediction tasks, it enables scalable application to large, uncharacterized human proteomes. Overall, G4SAINT provides a robust and extensible approach for systematic discovery of RG4-binding proteins, offering new opportunities for understanding RNA-protein interactions and identifying potential therapeutic targets. Our code and datasets are available at: https://github.com/o-nwn-o/G4SAINT.

title: Model-agnostic solutions for deep reinforcement learning in non-ergodic contexts.
authors: Bert Verbruggen; Arne Vanhoyweghen; Vincent Ginis
journal: Philosophical transactions. Series A, Mathematical, physical, and engineering sciences
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) remains a central optimization framework in machine learning. Although RL agents can converge to optimal solutions, the definition of 'optimality' depends on the environment's statistical properties. The Bellman equation, central to most RL algorithms, is formulated in terms of expected values of future rewards. However, when ergodicity is broken, long-term outcomes depend on the specific trajectory rather than on the ensemble average. In such settings, the ensemble average diverges from the time-average growth experienced by individual agents, with expected-value formulations yielding systematically suboptimal policies. Prior studies demonstrated that traditional RL architectures fail to recover the true optimum in non-ergodic environments. We extend this analysis to deep RL implementations and show that these, too, produce suboptimal policies under non-ergodic dynamics. We show that this limitation can be addressed by treating non-ergodic decision problems as finite trajectory-exposure problems rather than as isolated one-step optimization tasks. By exposing the agent to compounded trajectories during training, the learned value estimates become more consistent with the process's intrinsic time growth. This improvement does not require altering the environmental feedback, such as reward transformations or modified objective functions, but arises naturally from the agent's exposure to temporal trajectories. Our results contribute to the growing body of research on RL methods for non-ergodic systems. This article is part of the theme issue 'Ergodicity and ergodicity breaking in the sciences'.

title: Chemically modified electrode-based electrochemical sensing platforms for machine learning-assisted chemo/bio-analysis applications.
authors: Rijun Gui; Hui Jin
journal: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
abstract: During the past decade, machine learning (ML) with powerful learning abilities has profoundly influenced the development trends of electrochemical sensors (ECSs). ML learns complex patterns from massive data to systematically improve the performance and application scope of ECSs from multiple levels, involving signal calibration, material design and system integration. Especially in the field of traditional chemically modified electrode-based electrochemical sensors (CME-ECSs), the applications of ML and deep learning (DL) have penetrated into various aspects of CME-ECS technology. Thus, this present review systematically summarizes research progress in the field of ML-assisted CME-ECSs, and highlights ML-assisted analysis applications, primarily including analysis applications of classification models and regression models based on supervised learning algorithms, analysis applications of dimensionality reduction models and clustering models based on unsupervised learning algorithms, and analysis applications of AI models based on DL or other ML algorithms. By introducing the latest and representative application examples of CME-ECSs, this review discusses in detail different scenarios of ML-assisted analysis applications. Meanwhile, rational comments are made on the design, preparation and performance of ML-assisted CME-ECSs, the optimization of ML/DL algorithms and models, the integration of ML and CME-ECSs, the analysis of performance optimization and expansion of application scenarios. This review is a timely, comprehensive and in-depth summary based on ML-assisted analysis applications, which will powerfully contribute to the development of ECSs in the crucial aspects of design, preparation, performance optimization and intelligent applications.

title: From classical signal detection theory to modern probabilistic classifiers: a review and unifying perspective for imaging science.
authors: Mark A Anastasio
abstract:
Signal detection theory (SDT) has long provided the foundation for task-based image quality assessment and observer modeling in medical image science. Modern learning systems, by contrast, are typically framed as probabilistic classifiers trained via empirical risk minimization. This review clarifies that these perspectives can be understood within a common Bayesian decision-theoretic framework.
We present classical hypothesis testing and Bayesian risk minimization alongside modern probabilistic learning, demonstrating that optimal detection reduces to estimating decision-relevant conditional quantities-including likelihood ratios, posterior probabilities, or predictive response distributions-and applying an action rule determined by priors and losses. We connect strictly proper scoring rules (e.g., cross-entropy) to posterior estimation, clarify the distinction between discrimination [receiver operating characteristic (ROC)/area under the ROC curve] and calibration (probability accuracy), interpret ROC geometry via Bayes risk, and relate classical model observers to logistic regression and deep networks. Extensions to multiclass detection and observer-constrained information measures are discussed.
In the binary setting, for fixed priors, the likelihood ratio and posterior probability encode the same ordering information, related by Bayes' rule. Strictly proper scoring rules provide a mechanism by which empirical risk minimization targets posterior probabilities at the population-risk optimum, thereby approximating the ideal observer statistic under suitable assumptions on the data-generating distribution, model class, optimization, and labels. Discrimination and calibration emerge as complementary but distinct properties: ROC analysis assesses ranking, whereas calibrated probabilities are required for principled threshold selection, prevalence adaptation, and clinical risk communication. Predictive V  -information is highlighted as an observer-dependent image quality metric enabled by access to predictive distributions.
Classical SDT and modern probabilistic classification are complementary implementations of a shared decision-theoretic structure centered on decision-relevant conditional quantities. Recognizing the separation between inference and decision, the distinction between discrimination and calibration, and the role of observer constraints when estimating task-specific information provides conceptual clarity and practical guidance for evaluating and deploying learning-enabled imaging pipelines.

title: A Pilot Within-Subject Study of the Feasibility, Acceptability, and Preliminary Learning Outcomes of AI-Assisted and Manual Concept Mapping Among Anesthesia Technology Students in Small-Group Settings.
authors: Sara Bahramnejad; Parinaz Jalalkamali; Elnaz Jalalkamali; Maryam Aalaa; Ali Shenaee; Mohadeseh Ahmadlou
journal: Advances in medical education and practice
abstract:
Concept mapping is an effective strategy for organizing information and promoting deep learning in medical education. However, the feasibility and acceptability of manual vs AI-assisted concept mapping in small-group settings, particularly in anesthesia education, remain unclear. This pilot study aimed to explore the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary learning outcomes of manual and AI-assisted concept mapping among anesthesia technology students in small-group settings.
In this quasi-experimental pilot study, 25 anesthesia students participated in manual and AI-assisted concept-mapping sessions. Learning outcomes were assessed using pre-test and post-test, and satisfaction using a researcher-developed, validated 13-item questionnaire. Data were analyzed using paired t-tests and a linear mixed-effects model (p < 0.05).
Learning scores improved significantly in manual concept mapping (3.55 ± 1.44 to 6.95 ± 1.62; p < 0.001; Cohen's d = 1.568), but not in the AI-assisted concept mapping (5.36 ± 2.04 to 6.14 ± 2.10; p = 0.234; d = 0.261). The time-by-condition interaction was significant (B = 2.54, 95% CI: 1.10-3.98; p < 0.001), indicating greater improvement in manual concept mapping. Overall satisfaction did not differ significantly (p = 0.085).
Learning outcomes improved significantly in the manual concept mapping condition, whereas the improvement in the AI-assisted condition was not statistically significant. The mixed-effects analysis also indicated a significantly greater pre-to-post learning gain in the manual concept mapping than in the AI-assisted concept mapping. Satisfaction was comparable between methods. These preliminary findings should be interpreted cautiously because method, topic, and order were confounded.

title: Application of artificial intelligence in predicting periodontal risks in orthodontic patients: a scoping review.
authors: Huishun Yang; Qianying He; Dongxu Hu
abstract:
This scoping review aims to evaluate artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning, for predicting periodontal risks in orthodontic patients and to identify methodological gaps limiting clinical translation.
Reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR and PRISMA-S guidelines, a systematic search was conducted across six electronic databases (PubMed, IEEE Xplore, Web of Science, Scopus, Embase, Cochrane Library), grey literature, and citation tracking (Jan 1, 2018-June 1, 2025). Out of 880 identified records (312 duplicates removed; 568 screened), 56 full texts were evaluated, yielding 3 core clinical CBCT studies meeting strict eligibility criteria (Xu et al., 2024; Pirayesh et al., 2024; Zheng et al., 2025). Methodological quality and risk of bias were appraised using QUADAS-2 and PROBAST.
Reported performance for orthodontically induced inflammatory root resorption (OIIRR) ranged from 82.1% accuracy in small canine-induced resorption cohorts to >94% accuracy in larger grading frameworks. However, critical appraisal revealed a high risk of bias across all studies due to single-center retrospective designs, lack of independent external validation, and missing calibration metrics. Direct clinical evidence for AI prediction of gingival recession or orthodontic alveolar bone loss was insufficient within strict pre-cutoff parameters.
While AI demonstrates technical feasibility for assessing orthodontically related root resorption risk, robust individual-level risk prediction remains unestablished. Prospective multicenter external validation and adherence to standardized reporting guidelines are required prior to routine clinical adoption.

title: Salivary glands auto-segmentation in head and neck radiotherapy: imaging modalities, models, and clinical relevance.
authors: Wing Lam Wong; Ching Yi Shum; Yee Lam Chow; Ka Hei Man; Helen K W Law; Shing Yau Tam
abstract: Radiotherapy-induced salivary gland injury is a major contributor to xerostomia and impaired quality of life in patients with head and neck cancer, making accurate organ-at-risk delineation clinically important. Deep learning-based auto-segmentation has the potential to improve contouring efficiency and consistency, but reported performance is heterogeneous and its clinical significance is not always clear. This narrative review summarizes current evidence on salivary gland auto-segmentation across computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and prostate-specific membrane antigen positron emission tomography-computed tomography (PSMA PET-CT), with particular emphasis on gland-specific challenges, performance evaluation, and clinical translation. CT has the largest evidence base and remains most relevant to routine radiotherapy planning, whereas MRI provides improved soft-tissue visualization and PSMA PET-CT offers high functional contrast for selected salivary structures. Across modalities, segmentation performance is generally more challenging for smaller structures, particularly the sublingual and tubarial gland regions. Importantly, geometric metrics such as the Dice similarity coefficient do not alone establish clinical acceptability or dosimetric equivalence; evaluation should also consider boundary accuracy, expert correction burden, clinical acceptability, and dosimetric impact. Current evidence is further limited by heterogeneous study designs and reference standards, scarce external validation, and limited evidence linking auto-segmentation directly to treatment-related toxicity or patient outcomes. Future research should prioritize multi-institutional validation, clinically meaningful evaluation, improved segmentation of small glands, and human-in-the-loop integration into adaptive radiotherapy. Overall, auto-segmentation represents a promising tool for salivary gland delineation, but its clinical implementation should be supported by evidence extending beyond geometric accuracy alone.

title: 3D Modeling Optimization with Artificial Intelligence.
authors: Mehmet Altug
abstract: This study aims to examine the differences between parametric modeling (Pm) and automatic surface modeling (ASm) methods in terms of dimensional accuracy and precision in designs. A component with amorphous, cylindrical, and flat surfaces was chosen as the sample. Fused Deposition Method (FDM) and Polyjet methods were used in 3D printers using the nominal data of this component. A 3D scanner was then used to scan the parts in question. These scans were remodeled with two different modeling methods, Pm and ASm. After modeling, the measured scan data were compared with the nominal data. In addition, the results of the study were optimized with the help of deep learning (DL) and extreme learning machines (ELM). The performance of the model created in DL and ELM was quite close to the actual performance. This result shows the validity of the optimization study. DL r 2 value was determined as 0.9774 (%97,74). The most effective results with DL optimization were obtained by using Adam as the optimization algorithm, ReLU as the activation function, 2 hidden layers, 20 neurons, and 20% of the data for testing. As a result, the lowest mean squared error (MSE) of 1.011 × 10-6 was obtained in DL. The results can serve as a guide for the use of DL in new projects. However, when these results were optimized with ELM, the MSE value was 1.011 × 10-6 and the r 2 value was 0.9748 (%97,48). To compare the optimization results, they were also optimized with ANN and linear regression. In linear regression, MSE value was calculated as 1.484 × 10-6 and r 2 value as 0.9677 (%96,77). This shows that ELM gave very successful prediction results as the most effective optimization. The points examined in the study were obtained from three different surface structures, including plane, cylindrical, and amorphous surfaces. In the results of this study, it will be extremely important and easy to determine the modeling method according to the type of surface to be studied, depending on the data.

title: AI-enabled gas sensors for breath-based diagnostics: smart mask platforms toward personalized healthcare.
authors: Rahul Suresh Ghuge; Jeena George; Venkatramaiah Nutalapati; Yuvaraj Sivalingam; Corrado Di Natale; Kiran Mangalampalli
abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) with breath-based gas detection is paving the way for promising advances in noninvasive diagnostics at the point of care. Specific volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in exhaled human breath act as biomarkers of several diseases. However, accurate breath analysis remains challenging because VOC concentrations vary from parts per billion (ppb) to parts per million (ppm). Conventional gas sensors suffer from humidity interference, baseline drift, signal noise, poor selectivity and sensor variability. AI enables robust pattern recognition, feature extraction and classification with improved accuracy. This review discusses how machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and the Internet of Things (IoT) transform conventional gas sensors into intelligent breath-monitoring devices. We review face-mask integration strategies, including fibre embedded, directly fabricated, and externally attached modular designs for real-time monitoring. We further discuss sensing materials, device architecture, data acquisition systems, cloud and edge computing platforms and ML and DL algorithms for disease prediction and wearable deployment. We also examine commercialization challenges, including the lack of universally accepted VOC biomarkers, the limited clinically validated datasets, privacy, model interpretability, and regulatory requirements. Finally, we highlight future directions toward clinically reliable, AI-enabled wearable breath diagnostic systems for personalized healthcare.

title: Machine learning-driven prediction of antimicrobial resistance in Staphylococcus aureus using genomic and allelic signatures.
authors: Joyeta Ghosh; Ravi Kant; Jyoti Taneja
abstract:
Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in Staphylococcus aureus is a growing clinical threat, and machine learning (ML) offers a scalable approach to identifying allele-level resistance determinants.
Using a dataset of 300 clinical isolates, we trained and compared seven ML models - LSTM, CNN, Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), Decision Tree, XGBoost, Logistic Regression, and Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) - to predict resistance across six clinically important antibiotics from allele, locus-tag, and EggNOG-annotation features. Training-set class imbalance was corrected with SMOTE and all seven models were retrained under one identical pipeline.
XGBoost achieved the strongest overall test-set performance (accuracy 95%, ROC AUC 0.9745, F1-score 0.9474), closely matched by Decision Tree (accuracy 95%, F1-score 0.9520). Both outperformed the deep-learning architectures (LSTM, CNN, MLP), which showed pronounced overfitting after class-imbalance correction. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis identified "cat__allele_Cluster_1015_Allele_8" as the most influential feature; this association is hypothesis-generating and reflects statistical importance within this dataset, not a confirmed causal or biological mechanism.
The genomic feature set was selected once, on the full isolate collection, by a prior SVM-RFE pipeline before the present train/test split, and no external, temporal, or multi-center validation dataset was used. Reported performance should therefore be read as an upper-bound, best-case estimate rather than a validated benchmark. These findings support ML, and ensemble methods such as XGBoost and Decision Tree in particular, as candidate components of future AMR surveillance and diagnostic pipelines, pending external and prospective validation.

title: Deep learning-based blood glucose prediction in pediatric type 1 diabetes patients exercising in free-living conditions.
authors: Yessine Zghal; Marzia Angela Cremona; Mélanie Henderson; Monia Rekik
abstract: This paper evaluates deep learning models for blood glucose prediction in children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes using insulin pumps and investigates whether transfer learning from adult data improves prediction accuracy and safety. Models were trained using data from the Type 1 Diabetes Exercise Initiative Pediatric study (84 pediatric insulin pump users) and its adult counterpart (380 adult insulin pump users). Two transfer learning strategies were compared: one using pediatric data only and another pre-training the model on adult data before fine-tuning it on the pediatric cohort and each target patient. Prediction accuracy and clinical safety were assessed using root mean square error (RMSE) and the Clarke Error Grid (CEG) at 10-, 20-, and 30-min prediction horizons, with results analyzed separately for open-loop and closed-loop users. Pre-training on adult data yielded the best performance. At 30 min, mean RMSE was 19.61 mg/dL (1.09 mmol/L), with at least 92.64% of predictions falling within zone A of the CEG for 75% of patients. No predictions fell within the unsafe zone E. Delayed hypoglycemia detection occurred only in a small subset of patients and was mainly associated with missing contextual information or atypical clinical events. An additional evaluation on pediatric patients treated with multiple daily injections (MDI) demonstrated clinically acceptable prediction accuracy and safety, supporting the applicability of the proposed transfer learning approach to MDI users. These findings demonstrate that transfer learning from adult data effectively mitigates pediatric data scarcity and enables accurate, clinically safe blood glucose prediction under free-living conditions.

title: Processing strategies for improving cortical thickness correspondence between low-field and high-field MRI in young people.
authors: Sunah Choi; Julia Shaw; Rebecca Cooper; Mary Corcoran; Soumya Sathe; Rebecca A Hayes; Isabelle Elder; Alfredo Lucas; Chetan Vadali; Joel M Stein; Maria Jalbrzikowski
abstract: Portable low-field MRI systems are a promising complement to conventional high-field systems, enabling broader access to MRI. However, correspondence in cortical thickness estimates between low- and high-field MRI in young people remains limited despite its importance for neurodevelopment and psychopathology. To evaluate how multiple low-field image processing approaches improve cortical thickness correspondence with high-field MRI in a large sample of young individuals, we collected T1-weighted (T1w) and T2-weighted (T2w) data using both low-field (64 mT) and high-field (3T) MRI within 1 week of each other from a community sample of young people. We applied deep learning-based super-resolution methods (SynthSR v1 and SynthSR v2) followed by recon-all, or other reconstruction methods (recon-all-clinical and recon-any), to low-field data acquired across multiple sequences (T1w and T2w) and orientations (axial, coronal, sagittal, and multi-orientation average), with and without resampling and/or co-registration. We assessed global, lobar, and regional cortical thickness correspondence with 3T MRI measures based on the Desikan-Killiany atlas using Pearson and intraclass correlations. We compared pipelines using Steiger's Z-tests and Fisher's Z-tests. A total of 150 individuals (mean age, 18.63 ± 5.07 years; 80 female) were included. We observed the highest global correspondence with recon-all-clinical applied to coronal T1w images (r = 0.40, p FDR = 3.02e-05), which significantly exceeded the best global correspondence in our previous study (Fisher's Z = 1.99, p = 0.047). At the lobar and regional levels, multi-orientation T2w images processed with recon-all-clinical showed the highest correspondence across the greatest number of regions (4/12 lobes; 13/68 regions). This pipeline showed the highest correspondence and largest improvements relative to recon-all alone in frontal, cingulate, and temporal regions, including the right pars triangularis (r = 0.52, p FDR = 4.78e-11; Steiger's Z = 4.78, p FDR = 4.25e-06), right caudal anterior cingulate (r = 0.47, p FDR = 3.83e-09; Steiger's Z = 5.46, p FDR = 1.32e-07), and left parahippocampal regions (r = 0.58, p FDR = 2.98e-14; Steiger's Z = 5.17, p FDR = 6.01e-07). We observed significantly improved cortical thickness correspondence in low-field MRI in young people relative to recon-all alone and our prior work. The recon-all-clinical pipeline yielded moderate correspondence, particularly in frontal, cingulate, and temporal regions. Our results demonstrate a methodological improvement in the use of low-field MRI for assessing cortical thickness in young people, providing a quantitative benchmark for current tools in this area.

title: Deep reinforcement learning-driven model-based adaptive PID strategy for six-wheeled rocker-bogie mobile platform.
authors: Hua Tian; Ya Tu; Hongxue Feng
abstract:
Six-wheel rocker-bogie rovers encounter nonlinear dynamics, variable traction, and wheel slip that can degrade the performance of fixed-gain proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controllers. This study develops a hybrid deep reinforcement learning-PID framework to improve steering and drive control under these conditions.
Two Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) actor-critic agents adapt the steering and drive PID gains online using low-level dynamic feedback. The reward functions penalise tracking errors, wheel slip, inter-joint mismatch, and abrupt control variations. The framework was evaluated in a three-dimensional MATLAB Simscape Multibody environment incorporating suspension articulation, wheel-terrain contact, and load redistribution. Comparisons with conventional PID and standard DDPG-PID controllers examined tracking accuracy, learning convergence, actuator responses, and disturbance rejection.
The proposed framework demonstrated more consistent learning convergence, reduced tracking deviations, and smoother actuator torque responses than the baseline controllers. Online gain adaptation improved the steering and drive responses under simulated variations in traction, slip, and payload distribution. The shaped rewards reduced fluctuations in gain updates and critic estimates.
These simulation findings support the potential of reinforcement learning-based PID gain adaptation for low-level control of rocker-bogie rovers under uncertain operating conditions. The framework retains the conventional PID structure while introducing data-driven adaptation. Hardware-in-the-loop testing and physical rover experiments remain necessary to establish performance beyond simulation.

title: Application of artificial intelligence in the diagnosis and treatment of thyroid cancer.
authors: Zhen Su; Shuo Wang; Xintao Wang; Wenjing Yao; Yanshu Li; Hao Wang; Jie Wang; Meng Jia
abstract: Thyroid cancer is one of the most common endocrine malignancies, and its rising incidence has increased the demand for more accurate and efficient diagnostic and management strategies. Current clinical management mainly relies on ultrasonography, fine-needle aspiration (FNA), surgery, radioactive iodine therapy, thyroid-stimulating hormone suppression, and systemic treatment in selected advanced cases. However, substantial interobserver variability, indeterminate cytology, and heterogeneity in tumor behavior still complicate diagnosis and risk stratification. In thyroid cancer, AI(Artificial intelligence) -assisted models have been applied to ultrasound, CT, MRI, cytology, histopathology, and genomic data, with promising performance in distinguishing benign from malignant nodules, predicting lymph node metastasis and key mutations, and supporting individualized management. This review critically synthesizes evidence across these applications, focusing on study design, validation strategies, generalizability, and clinical relevance. It also examines explainable AI, emerging foundation models, and regulatory and implementation challenges. Although many models report high diagnostic or predictive performance, these results alone do not establish improvements in clinical decision-making or patient outcomes. Prospective clinical validation, cost-effectiveness assessment, and evaluation of integration into clinical workflows are needed to determine whether AI provides meaningful benefits over standard care.

title: Generalizing ECG-based fatigue detection across fatigue-induction paradigms using deep learning.
authors: Ludmila Kralikova; Juraj Spanik; Branko Babusiak
abstract:
Fatigue and sleepiness can arise under different experimental and behavioral conditions, yet ECG-based detection models are often evaluated only within the dataset used for development. This study investigated the participant-independent and cross-dataset performance of two ECG-derived approaches: a 1D CNN based on six HRV features and a dual-input CNN-BiLSTM combining RR interval sequences with statistical HRV descriptors.
Models were developed using the DROZY database, in which sleepiness was induced by prolonged wakefulness. Internal performance was assessed using five-fold subject-wise evaluation on 25 recordings from 14 participants. The models were then applied without retraining or parameter adaptation to the independent FatiQData dataset comprising 20 participants performing a prolonged monotonous driving task.
On DROZY, the HRV-based 1D CNN achieved 60.0% accuracy, 61.5% F1-score, and a ROC-AUC of 0.593, whereas the dual-input CNN-BiLSTM achieved 68.0% accuracy, 73.3% F1-score, and a ROC-AUC of 0.753. In FatiQData, Stanford Sleepiness Scale scores increased significantly from 2.40 ± 0.82 to 4.15 ± 0.81. For binary external discrimination, the HRV-based model achieved 60.0% accuracy, 69.2% F1-score, and a ROC-AUC of 0.766, while the dual-input model achieved 65.0% accuracy, 77.4% F1-score, and a ROC-AUC of 0.750.
The results indicate that ECG-derived HRV and RR dynamics retain information related to subjective sleepiness, while participant-independent and cross-dataset performance remains moderate. These findings emphasize the importance of subject-wise validation, independent external testing, and cautious interpretation across heterogeneous experimental conditions.

title: Predicting Cardiac Arrest Using Ultrasound and MRI Images: A Multimodal Machine Learning Approach on Left Ventricular Myocardium Parameters.
authors: P Katheeja Khanam; V Anantha Natarajan
abstract:
Sudden Cardiac Arrest (SCA) is a life-threatening cardiovascular emergency, with survival rates below 10% without immediate intervention. Accurate prediction requires comprehensive characterization of left ventricular (LV) myocardial structure and function, which cannot be fully captured by a single imaging modality. This study proposes MuMo-CardNet, a multimodal deep learning framework for SCA risk prediction using complementary echocardiography and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).
The proposed five-stage pipeline integrates 2D echocardiography from the CAMUS dataset and short-axis cine MRI from the ACDC dataset. The framework performs image preprocessing, deep feature extraction using transfer-learned ResNet-50 encoders, dimensionality reduction through Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE), and cross-modal fusion using a Variational Autoencoder with Cross-Attention Transformer (VAE-CAT). XGBoost is subsequently employed for classification. A harmonization module projects heterogeneous imaging features into a common representational space.
MuMo-CardNet achieved a 93.7% reduction in inter-modality Kullback-Leibler divergence, indicating effective harmonization of heterogeneous imaging characteristics. On a merged test dataset of 271 subjects, the model achieved an AUC-ROC of 0.967, accuracy of 96.5%, and F1-score of 0.945, outperforming single-modality and simple feature-concatenation approaches. Based on the findings, it is clear that MuMo-CardNet is capable of delivering reliable and explainable risk stratification for cardiac diseases using echocardiography and cardiac MRI features. This is because of the discriminatory and sensitive nature of MuMo-CardNet that makes it suitable for use in early identification of cardiac risks.
SHAP-based interpretation identified Ejection Fraction, End Diastolic Volume, and Wall Motion Score as the most influential predictors, providing clinically consistent feature-level explanations. The framework demonstrates the potential of multimodal imaging fusion for accurate and interpretable SCA risk prediction.

title: Objective assessment and virtual lesion simulation of psoriasis lesion severity based on deep learning regression and generative models.
authors: Liuyan Zhu; Zhuoran Ma; Haotian Qian; Yuwen Zhang; Peiyao Zheng
abstract:
The Psoriasis Area and Severity Index (PASI) remains the gold standard for evaluating psoriasis severity; however, the assessment of its subscores-erythema, scaling, and induration-relies heavily on clinicians' subjective judgment, leading to poor inter-rater consistency. This study aims to develop an objective evaluation model, Psoriasis-RegNet, based on deep learning regression, using publicly available dermatological image repositories, and to explore a conditional generative model, Psoriasis-GAN, for creating virtual lesion simulations of psoriasis lesions and demonstrating their potential applications in medical education.
A total of 1,250 clinical images of psoriasis were collected from the public DermNet dermatology image archive. Based on the accompanying clinical descriptions, a large pre-trained language-vision model was employed to automatically annotate each image with erythema (E), scaling (S), and induration (I) scores on a 0-4 scale, thereby constructing a multi-label regression dataset. The reliability of the pseudo-labels was evaluated against independent annotations from board-certified dermatologists, yielding ICC values of 0.86, 0.83, and 0.79 for erythema, scaling, and induration, respectively. (1) Psoriasis-RegNet: We developed a multi-task regression network using ResNet-50 as the backbone, pretrained on the ISIC 2019 skin lesion dataset. Three independent regression heads were attached to predict the E, S, and I scores, respectively, enabling simultaneous quantitative evaluation of lesion severity components. (2) Psoriasis-GAN: We further implemented a conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN) based on the StyleGAN2-ADA architecture. The composite vector E,S,I was used as the conditional input to guide the generation of high-resolution psoriasis lesion images, supporting controllable and clinically meaningful visual synthesis.
The Psoriasis-RegNet model demonstrated excellent performance on the held-out internal test set. The mean absolute errors (MAE) for erythema, scaling, and induration predictions were 0.42, 0.45, and 0.48, respectively. The Pearson correlation coefficients (PCC) between model predictions and the held-out reference labels were 0.85, 0.82, and 0.80 for erythema, scaling, and induration, respectively (all P < 0.001). These prediction errors are within the range of inter-rater variability reported among dermatologists for PASI subscores (typical MAE: 0.5-0.9). The Psoriasis-GAN successfully generated high-fidelity (1,024 × 1,024) and conditionally controllable lesion images, achieving a Frechet Inception Distance (FID) of 28.5, and a Visual Turing Test discrimination accuracy of 51.3 percent, indicating near-photorealistic quality.
This study demonstrates that re-annotation of public dermatological image repositories provides a feasible approach for developing AI models in dermatology. The proposed Psoriasis-RegNet offers an objective and quantitative tool for psoriasis severity assessment, while Psoriasis-GAN shows great potential for medical education and AI data augmentation through the creation of virtual lesion simulations that enable interactive exploration of psoriasis severity phenotypes.

title: RELATION OF HEART WEIGHT WITH AGE AND WEIGHT OF CADAVER
authors: Jolly Agarwal; Virendra Kumar
abstract: Introduction: Height, weight, and age of person has significant impact on the normal size of heart. These parameters need to be considered when cut-off values indicating the need for treatment or even surgery are established. The aim of present work is to study the relation of weight of the heart with age and weight of cadaver. Material and Methods: The study was performed in the Department of Anatomy, Shri Ram Murti Smarak Institute of Medical Sciences, Bareilly on 30 hearts from embalmed cadavers. The hearts were procured from the cadavers available in our department. The heart was thoroughly cleaned and measurements were taken. Results: The mean heart weight was 223.37 ± 57.78 g. Significant relationship between age of the cadaver and weight of the heart (p=0.0004), weight of cadaver and weight of heart (p=0.0001) was observed. Conclusion: The above study provides valuable data of the heart in our geographical location, which may be useful for cardiac surgeons and physicians.
